CVE-2026-102615.title: HeyForm: Uploaded HTML files are served as text/html on the app origin with no CSP — stored XSS
CVE-2026-102615.description: HeyForm is an open-source form builder. Prior to 3.0.1, /api/upload accepts a file according to the client-controlled multipart file.mimetype while retaining an HTML filename, and static/upload serves the resulting file as text/html with contentSecurityPolicy: false. An ordinary user can therefore upload active HTML that executes on the HeyForm origin when a victim opens its returned URL. The same-origin script can access /graphql with the victim's session and read or modify data available to that account. The code also permits upload requests tied to an active public form through formId, openToken, and a fieldId belonging to a file or signature question, although the advisory did not fully verify that unauthenticated path end to end. This issue is fixed in version 3.0.1.

CVE-2026-102884.title: Connaisseur: Cosign multi-signature threshold bypass through repeated signatures from one trust root
CVE-2026-102884.description: Connaisseur is an admission controller that integrates container image signature verification into a Kubernetes cluster. Prior to 3.11.1, the Cosign validator counts valid signature layers rather than distinct trust roots for trustRoot: "*" policies using an explicit threshold or an implicit require-all policy. An attacker who controls one configured trust root's signing key and can attach multiple signatures to an image can satisfy a threshold intended to require multiple independent roots, causing admission without the intended signer quorum. Policies using a single trust root or the required option are not affected. This issue is fixed in 3.11.1.

CVE-2026-119237.description: In proxygen's HTTP/3 session, when a HEADERS block referenced QPACK dynamic table entries that had not yet been received, header decoding for that stream was paused, but the session continued to read the stream from the QUIC transport. The unread data bypassed the session's ingress buffer limit, returned flow-control credit to the peer, and was re-scanned in full on every read. With QPACK blocked streams enabled (the default), a remote, unauthenticated HTTP/3 peer could send a HEADERS block that references a dynamic table insert it never sends, followed by a continuous stream of data, causing memory growth until the request timed out and CPU usage that grows quadratically, leading to denial of service. CVE-2026-99030.title: net: skbuff: don't leave stale bytes in skb_copy_and_csum_bits()
CVE-2026-99030.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: skbuff: don't leave stale bytes in skb_copy_and_csum_bits()

When skb_copy_and_csum_bits() reaches unreadable frags it returns 0
after copying only the linear part, and the rest of the caller's buffer
is left as it was. The callers copy into a buffer that is about to go
out on the wire: an ICMP error quoting the offending packet, or a
driver's TX bounce buffer in skb_copy_and_csum_dev(). Neither buffer
is zeroed beforehand, so whatever was in memory there gets sent.

Zero the part of the buffer we didn't fill. The checksum usually
won't match the data any more, so the receiver will usually drop the
packet, but either way it no longer carries anything it shouldn't.
Only zero for a positive @len, a negative one from a broken caller must
not turn into a huge memset().

CVE-2026-99045.title: ibmveth: h_free logical LAN on open-fail after register
CVE-2026-99045.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ibmveth: h_free logical LAN on open-fail after register

ibmveth_open() registers the logical LAN, then allocates the RX
buffer pools. A pool failure jumps to out_free_buffer_pools without
h_free_logical_lan(), so PHYP still owns the buffer-list page when
it is unmapped. request_irq() failure already issued the hypercall
before taking the same label.

Move that h_free to the shared post-register unwind so both paths
deregister before the buffer list is unmapped.

filelock: keep superblock active through delegation wait

A caller may drop its path after try_break_deleg() returns a delegated
inode but before break_deleg_wait() finishes. The extra inode reference
held in struct delegated_inode does not keep the superblock active.

After a lazy unmount, closing the delegation holder can release the last
mount reference and shut down the superblock while another task waits for
the delegation break. The waiter's final iput() can then enter the
filesystem's eviction code after its superblock-private state was freed.
This has been observed as a KASAN use-after-free in shmem_evict_inode().

When try_break_deleg() saves a delegated inode, take an active reference
to its superblock while the caller still pins the mount. Keep that
reference through break_deleg_wait() and the final iput(), then release
it with deactivate_super(). This protects every caller of the helpers,
including the…

CVE-2026-99492.title: HID: wacom: Advertise SW_MUTE_DEVICE capability prior to registration
CVE-2026-99492.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

HID: wacom: Advertise SW_MUTE_DEVICE capability prior to registration

Input subsystem guidelines require that device capabilities are advertised
before the input device is registered. The Wacom driver was violating
this by advertising the SW_MUTE_DEVICE capability post-registration in
wacom_set_shared_values() (and duplicating it in device-specific setup
cases).

Resolve this by moving the SW_MUTE_DEVICE capability setup to
wacom_setup_touch_input_capabilities() for all touch devices that support
it.

For generic touch devices whose capabilities depend on mute switch
usages parsed from a sibling Pen/Pad interface, defer registration
with -EPROBE_DEFER until the sibling has parsed its descriptors and
initialized shared capabilities.
